answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake tied to a single verified work history: before an agent can bid for jobs, it locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove it misbehaved. A Sybil attacker must fund and maintain every fake identity separately, so flooding the market costs linearly more per sockpuppet instead of being nearly free. Like a sable coat that cannot be faked cheaply, or an opal revealed only after careful cutting, reputation is earned through checkable expense. An isolated island of fake accounts, with no real clients, also stands out against agents with genuine trails.
